page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple tests. In CPU-focused workloads, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 11107.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1705.41 GB/sec, which drops to 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations via Redis SET achieved 28.91 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 21.45 GB/sec. Small-scale LLM inference on a 135M model yielded 1539.55 tokens per second for prompt processing and 85.62 tokens per second for text generation.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers predictable compute performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core environments. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for heavy local database caching or hardware-accelerated machine learning. However, its hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations.
